description.narrative:
IVI:s främsta syfte är att utveckla vaccin mot sjukdomar som främst drabbar människor som lever i fattigdom, för att därigenom främja en förbättrad global folkhälsa. De arbetar också med att möjliggöra vaccination, bland annat genom att ta fram data över effektivitet, sjukdomsspridning och antimikrobiell resistens och genom att stötta länders regulatoriska system i låg- och medelinkomstländer (LMIC). Genom vaccination och efterföljande minskning av sjukdomsbördan finns en rad positiva effekter för samhället i stort.
IVIs vision är utvecklingsländer fria från infektionssjukdomar. För att åstadkomma detta, utvecklar IVI vaccin mot just infektionssjukdomar med stor vikt för global folkhälsa och vars bot har begränsad kommersiell potential.
Deras nuvarande strategi, 2022-2026, har tre huvudsakliga mål:
- Förstärka IVIs kärnverksamhet: forskning och utveckling, inklusive laboratorieforskning, tekniköverföring, klinisk vaccinutveckling, epidemiologi och övervakning, vaccineffektivitet. Detta ihop med kapacitetsstärkande program och AMR-projekt.
- Skala upp det globala avtrycket: utöka internationell närvaro och öka antalet medlemsländer i IVI.
- Framtidssyftande styrning: Skapa en mer inkluderande och lyhörd styrningsstruktur genom att integrera fler IVI-medlemsstater i institutionell styrning.
Under kommande år, kommer flera nya kontor att etableras och driva sin egen lokalt anpassade verksamhet. IVI förväntas delta i allt fler globala sammanhang (ex WHO, Gavi, afrikanska vaccinsatsningar), de har flera vaccin i pipeline och genomför förändringen i styrning av institutet. Om fyra år kan vi räkna med två afrikanska kontor med etablerad närvaro i fler länder på kontinenten, en mera inkluderande styrningsstruktur och större ägarskap och ledarskap i länderna där arbetet genomförs. Utöver detta, en rad viktiga resultat inom vaccinutveckling, stöd till vaccinationsprogram på lokal nivå, och deltagande i en rad kliniska studier.
För 2025 bidrar Sida med extra medel för att stärka IVI:s etablering på den afrikanska kontinenten.

International Vaccine Institute, IVI, was established in 1997 as a multilateral research institute which develops vaccines in order to reduce the burden of poverty-related disease. IVI offers technical assistance to vaccine producers and regulators in low- and lower-middle-income countries, and maintains an international network of collaborating research institutions.
Sida has supported IVI since 2002, and provides non-earmarked program support to IVI's strategy implementation.

International Vaccine Institute, IVI, är en multilateral forskningsorganisation som grundades 1997. Verksamheten inriktas på att producera och sprida vaccin mot infektioner som främst drabbar de som lever i fattigdom, i synnerhet diarré- och luftvägssjukdomar. Sverige är signatärstat och medlem i IVI sedan 1997 (Regeringsbeslut 1996-12-19, UD96/1555/GC).
Institutet har samarbete med cirka 50 partners runtom i världen, vilka inkluderar forskningsinstitutioner och universitet, regeringar, läkemedelsföretag och vaccintillverkare. Dessa globala samarbeten och partnerskap bidrar till att säkerställa hållbar tillgång av effektiva och prisvärda vacciner för människor som lever i fattigdom.
Sida har stött IVI sedan 2002 med ett brett programstöd till institutets verksamhetsplan.

description.narrative:
(text in English as the contribution is handled by the Embassy of Sweden in Rwanda)
Results show that the International Vaccine Institute (IVI) is not only advancing science but also making sure vaccines are more affordable, accessible, and locally produced. By opening offices in Africa and Asia, IVI is bringing research closer to where its most needed. And by training hundreds of professionals, they are building the skills and systems that ensure vaccines reach people everywhere.
Since the start of Sida's support in January 2025 the following results, aligned with the IVI strategy, have been achieved:
Strengthen IVIs Core Activities
(Discovery, development, delivery, capacity building)
- The microneedle array patch with HepB vaccine phase 1 trial (first in human) was fully enrolled with 40 healthy individuals.
- Malaria vaccine registration in DRC was supported and almost 3 500 participants are enrolled.
- IVI's "Vaccine number 4" program was initiated, aiming for a vaccine against Klebsiella pneumoniae.
- Clinical trial initiating for the tech-transferred cholera vaccine to South-African company Biovac (OCV-S, first ever manufacturing of full vaccine in Africa) in South Africa (see more https://healthpolicy-watch.news/south-africa-launches-trial-of-first-african-made-cholera-vaccine/). The OCV-S is an improved and simplified version of the cholera vaccine, and with the same investment 30% more vaccine can be manufactured to a 20% lower price.
- In addition, IVI is progressing towards an entercoated capsule of the cholera vaccine, which will be heat stable, have lower delivery costs, and lead to less waste.
Capacity strengthening
- IVI vaccinology course: the one-week training in vaccinology took place in three locations simultaneously in both 2024 and 2025 (Seoul, Stockholm and Kigali). Trainers are present in all three locations, and recordings were shared online to accommodate for time differences. In Kigali 2025 there were around 85 participants from 15 countries (Nigeria, Somalia, DR Congo, Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya, Rwanda, Zambia, India, Germany, UK, Ethiopia...). Presenters were from public and private sectors, donors and multilaterals (WHO, Unicef). Sida did one of the welcome remarks at the Kigali site.
Important discussions were held around the outbreak of Marburg in Rwanda 2024: how this was handled and lessons learned. Rwandan authorities as well as WHO and CEPI were present. Although the outbreak was exceptionally handled, there was an interesting discussion on even faster protocols for clinical trials on vaccines.
- Global Training Hub for Biomanufacturing took place, providing workforce training in vaccine and biologics R&D and manufacturing for students and professionals from low- and middle-income countries.
- IVI hosted 2025 Introductory Course for Standard Practice (GxP) as part of WHO biomanufacturing training initiative, a three-week in-person program. It trained 192 international participants from 39 countries, along with 21 Korean participants from domestic biopharmaceutical companies and graduate programs. The trainees include professionals from organizations involved in the development and manufacturing of biopharmaceuticals such as vaccines, therapeutics, and monoclonal antibodies in LMICs.
- In connection to the IVI Board of Trustees meeting in Kigali November 2025, a symposium was organized by IVI and the University of Rwanda with world-leading global health experts. This opportunity was important in particular for MAV participants and others involved in vaccines R&D.
Scale Up the Global Footprint
- Establishment of the IVI African Regional Office in Kigali (IARO) with a Director and two team members (admin assistant and operations specialist).
- Recent establishment of the IVI Project Office in Nairobi with a Director (November).
- Hong Kong Jockey Club Global Health Institute (a joint initiative between IVI, Cambridge and Hong Kong University) was inaugurated in October
- New grants in 2025 (as of October) are almost 78 million USD.
- 60 countries and WHO have now joined as IVI members or are in process of joining.
Future-Oriented Governance
- As a result of the new offices, resulting in a new IVI structure, a new governance structure is being put in place. The IERO (European Regional Office) and IARO Directors are members of the IVI leadership team and report directly to the DG. The process is still ongoing.
- A risk management unit was established at HQ, and a number of activities were implemented such as a cybersecurity audit by KPMG.
- A risk coordination network shall be fully functional as of December 2025.
- IVI is ranked as a "high performer" in the Global 50/50 gender and health index.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
